Lemma: G1150

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "to tame, subdue, bring under control (of animals or the tongue)"
  Readable gloss: "Damazo means to subdue or tame what is wild and unruly. Mark 5:4 uses it of the Gerasene demoniac whom no one could restrain — not even chains could 'tame' him. James employs the word three times in his discourse on the tongue: every species of beast and bird has been tamed by humankind (Jas 3:7), yet no human being can tame the tongue (Jas 3:8). The contrast between humanity's mastery over nature and helplessness before its own speech makes for one of James's most striking arguments."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: ""
    Enriched: To tame, subdue, or bring under control what is wild or unruly. Applied to the demoniac whom no one could restrain (Mark 5:4), and used by James of humanity's ability to tame every animal species yet inability to tame the tongue (Jas 3:7-8). Spanish 'domar,' French 'dompter,' and German 'zaehmen' each carry the sense of mastering something fierce, reinforcing the image of overcoming wildness.
    Existing Spanish translations: domar, es-domada, ha-sido-domada

}
